comments.why_zh: 用一小时讲解现代开放寻址哈希表
comments.quote_zh: （警告，视频有一个小时。铺垫也要花一会儿。但仍然值得看。）
comments.text_zh: 我觉得你低估了链式哈希所需的内存重定向次数。不止一次。这才是致命的地方。要警惕一种假设：你的数据会在缓存里。通常并不在。问题不在于在哈希表里做大量高密度查找，问题在于时不时地做一次查找。一个要做三次 DRAM 访问的哈希表，永远比只做一次的要差，不管它需要做多少工作，原因有两个。第一点很明显：内存慢得要命，这我们知道。第二点更隐蔽。你刚刚逐出了两条缓存行。不只是查找本身变慢了，你还让你这个数据结构的消费者也变慢了。下面看看如今开放寻址是什么样子：[VIDEO]（警告，视频有一个小时。铺垫也要花一会儿。但仍然值得看。）
comments.text: I think you're underestimating the number of memory redirections that are necessary for chaining. It's more than one. That's the killer. It's important to be wary of assuming your data will be in cache. It usually isn't. The problem isn't making lots of high density searches in a hash map, the problem is making a search every now and then. A hash map that makes three DRAM accesses will always be worse that one that makes one, regardless of how much work it needs to do, and this is for two reasons. First is there obvious: RAM is slow as balls, we get it. Second is more insidious. You just evicted two cache lines. It's not just the lookup itself that's slower, you also made the consumer of your data structure slower. Here's a look at what open addressing looks like these days: [VIDEO] (warning, it's an hour. Takes a while to build up, too. Still worth it.)

comments.why_zh: Abseil 对 SwissTable 的展示
comments.text_zh: 它们非常、非常相似。哈希是两层的：第一层相当传统。你从哈希里取前 k 位，然后在表里查它。第二层是 128 位块（一个 SSE/NEON 寄存器）。这个块包含 14 个 8 位块，其中最高位是墓碑标记，低 7 位是哈希里第 k+1 到 k+7 位（或者是最高 7 位？不确定。总之是哈希里没被上层用到的 7 位）。它用 SSE 指令来找出 14 个块里哪一个需要做完整的键比较。两者都有两个变体，一个保证即使迭代器失效，对键和值的引用仍然有效；另一个更快，但迭代器失效会让对键或值的引用也失效。恕我直言，看起来 Folly 团队去年看了 Abseil 的演讲后说：“好主意，我们也该这么做。” Abseil 演讲：[视频] 非常有意思。
comments.text: They are very, very similar. The hashes are two level: one is fairly traditional. You take the first k bits from the hash and look that up in a table. The second layer is 128 bit blocks. (one SSE/NEON register) This block contains 14 8 bit blocks, where the top bit is a tombstone marker, and the bottom 7 bits are the k+1 though k+7 bit from the hash. (or the top 7 bits? not sure. it's 7 bits from the hash that aren't used in the top layer) It uses SSE instructions to identify which of the 14 blocks to do a full key compare with. Both of them have two variants, one which guarantees that references to keys and values will remain valid even if iterators are invalidated, and another which is faster but iterator invalidation invalidates references to keys or values. IMHO it looks like the Folly team saw the Abseil presentation last year and said, "That's a good idea, we should do that." abseil presentation: [VIDEO] It's super interesting.

comments.author: kllrnohj
comments.why_zh: 密集扁平哈希集合设计
comments.quote_zh: 这里有一个关于这种密集扁平哈希集合的好演讲
comments.text_zh: 这里就进入了 O(1) != 快 的领域。算法复杂度和 CPU 性能之间关系很弱，不是强关系。如果你想在一个集合里查找，把它存成数组做线性扫描，由于 CPU 的工作方式，在数量多到令人吃惊的程度之前都会胜过 std::unordered_set。尤其是 std::unordered_set 的指针追逐问题会成为麻烦（大多数哈希集合实现都有这个问题）。记住，unordered_set 不是项目数组，而是项目桶的数组（哈希冲突就是这样处理的）。更糟的是，这些桶通常是链表。它通常既不能被有效推测执行，也不能被有效预取，所以在未命中缓存查找时，你会受限于内存延迟。而内存延迟差不多就是糟糕透顶。如果你预期查找能命中 L1/L2/L3 缓存，那你处理的规模可能不算很大，而且用扁平数组会比桶数组获得好得多的缓存密度。也有替代的哈希集合是扁平的、能避免这个问题，但它们不那么常见，据我所知，任何语言的标准实现都没有用这种哈希集合。这里有一个关于这种密集扁平哈希集合的好演讲：[视频]
comments.text: This is where we get into O(1) != fast territory. Algorithmic complexity has a weak relationship to CPU performance, not a strong one. If you want to find something in a set storing it as an array and doing a linear scan will beat a std::unordered_set up to a shockingly large number of items due to how CPU's work. In particular it's the pointer chasing aspect of std::unordered_set that becomes a problem (an issue shared with _most_ hash set implementations). Remember an unordered_set is not an array of items, it's an array of buckets of items (this is how hash collision is handled). Worse still, those buckets are usually linked lists. It typically can't be speculated effectively and it can't be prefetched effectively, so you become memory latency bound during an un-cached lookup. And memory latency is just shy of absolutely terrible. If you're expecting L1/L2/L3 cache hits on lookups then you're not dealing with vary large sizes probably and you're going to get much better cache density with the flat array than the array-of-buckets. There are alternative hashsets that are flat and avoid this, but they are less common and as far as I know no standard implementation on any language uses such a hash set. There's a good talk about such a dense, flat hash set here: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 他们用的数据集是小于 14GB 的 parquet [1]，所以这个“冷启动”似乎意在某种程度上也测量数据集无法完全装入内存的情况。我不认为这是疏忽，而只是他们发现这样做可行。这在 [1] 里写得很明确。另外，搭建这个 benchmark 的人对于在困难条件下做基准测试非常认真 [2]。我个人的看法是，你需要海量数据以及大量不同的变量来分别测试。比如，你可能想监控发生了多少次 cache miss/hit、p99 延迟等等。而且你要在满负载、预期负载等条件下做。你还想比较同一个数据库的不同版本，因为比较不同的数据库会让事情在组合上难得多——当然，除非你有一个真实的、正在针对其做优化的生产用例。Cppcon 上那个 swisstable 演讲就是一个很好的例子，说明了一个有用的基准测试和优化，也展示了要真正评估哪怕“很小”的改动带来的性能影响有多难。[3] [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [VIDEO]
comments.text: The dataset they use is <14GB of parquet [1] so the "cold start" seems to be intended to also measure having a dataset that doesn't fit in memory in a way. I don't think this is an oversight but it is just what they found to be feasible. This is explicitly written in [1]. Also the guy who setup this benchmark is very serious about benchmarking under difficult conditions [2] My personal opinion is that you need a massive amount of data and massive number of different variables to test for separately. For example you might want to monitor how many cache misses/hits there were, p99 latency etc. And you want to do it under full load, expected load etc. And you want to compare the different versions of the same database because comparing different databases makes things combinatorially more difficult, unless you have a real production use case that you are optimizing for ofc. The swisstable talk on cppcon is a good example of a useful benchmark and optimization that shows how difficult it is to really asses performance effects of even "small" changes.
